Metadata.title: VayuNetra: satellite methane screening for Indian landfills
Metadata.description: VayuNetra finds, verifies and measures methane plumes from Indian landfills in free Sentinel-2 imagery, then turns them into action dossiers for MoHUA, CPCB/SPCBs and municipal corporations.

Hero.eyebrow: Satellite AI for Indian landfill methane
Hero.title: Methane is invisible. VayuNetra makes it visible.
Hero.subtitle: Satellite AI that finds, verifies and measures methane from India's landfills — and turns it into action.

Problem.title: Landfill methane is large, fast-acting and mostly unmeasured
Problem.warming: Methane traps about {value} times more heat than CO₂ over 20 years.
Problem.warmingSource: IPCC AR6, GWP20 {gwp20} for non-fossil methane
Problem.maasakkers: Landfill emissions in Delhi, Mumbai, Lahore and Buenos Aires were {low}–{high} times higher than earlier estimates.
Problem.fire: Delhi's Ghazipur landfill caught fire. Fires and methane come from the same buried waste.
Problem.line: No one measures it landfill by landfill.

How.title: From a free satellite pass to an action dossier

pass.title: Sentinel-2 pass
pass.text: Free Sentinel-2 imagery arrives about every {days} days. Every new pass over a site is cut into a chip around the landfill.

mbmp.title: MBMP retrieval
mbmp.text: The multi-band multi-pass method compares the two shortwave-infrared bands with earlier clean passes of the same place.

ai.title: AI segmentation
ai.text: A U-Net with a {encoder} encoder, pretrained on Sentinel-2 ({pretraining}) and trained on {plumes} real plumes plus simulated ones, outlines the plume and scores the scene.

gate.title: Physics gate
gate.text: Methane darkens band 12 strongly, band 11 weakly and visible light not at all, and a plume lies along the wind. Fires, moisture and fresh waste fail these tests.

rate.title: kg/h with uncertainty
rate.text: The plume's integrated mass and the ERA5-Land wind give an emission rate with a 68% range. In calm wind no rate is reported.

dossier.title: Action dossier
dossier.text: Each site gets a dossier with the evidence, the rate and the next step for MoHUA, CPCB/SPCBs and the municipal corporation.

Proof.title: Global benchmark on held-out test sites
Proof.intro: VayuNetra against the classic MBMP method, scored on sites the model never saw in training.

auc.title: ROC AUC
auc.meaning: 0.5 is a coin toss: the score cannot tell plumes from clean scenes. The classic method scores {mbmp}, close to that. VayuNetra scores {vayunetra}.

recall.title: Recall by emission rate (t/h)
recall.meaning: Above 3 t/h VayuNetra finds 3 to 6 times more plumes than the classic method. Below 1 t/h it finds fewer: {low} against {lowMbmp}.

iou.title: Plume outline (pixel IoU)
iou.meaning: How well the drawn outline overlaps the true plume: {vayunetra} against {mbmp}, about four times closer.

accuracy.title: Emission rate within ±50%
accuracy.meaning: For {share} of {plumes} real plumes the estimated rate is within ±50% of the published MARS rate. The median ratio is {ratio}, so estimates are not biased high or low.

Proof.operating: At the operating threshold: precision {pV} vs {pM}, recall {rV} vs {rM}, false-alarm rate {fV} vs {fM}.

Honest.title: A free screener, then a confirmation
Honest.tier1Text: Sentinel-2, every new pass, every site. Finds candidates and rules out most surface changes.
Honest.tier2Text: Hyperspectral satellite, OGI drone or ground survey on the flagged cell.
Honest.boundsMeaning: A steady emitter at or above this rate would have produced more flags than we saw.

limits.perPass: Over dense Indian landfills a single pass catches about {share} of plumes of {tph} t/h or more.
limits.small: Below 1 t/h the model finds {recall} of plumes.
limits.finetune: Fine-tuning on Indian backgrounds did not improve held-out detection (AUC ≈ {auc}). The limit is the Sentinel-2 signal against dense urban backgrounds, which is why VayuNetra has two tiers.
limits.truth: In a known-truth test on an Indian background, the estimated rate was {ratio}× the injected rate at {tph} t/h.
limits.deonar: The Deonar T1 event stays unconfirmed until the hyperspectral check.
limits.screening: Every rate on this page is screening-grade.

Initiative.title: Why we built VayuNetra
Initiative.why: Landfill gas can be captured and burned for power, but only where someone has found it. Sentinel-2 is free and passes over every Indian city about every {days} days. We built VayuNetra to turn those passes into site-by-site evidence a municipal corporation or pollution control board can act on.
Initiative.teamText: Team lead: Jiyad Hussain, Amity University, Noida. Built for the Net Zero AI Architecture hackathon.
Initiative.openText: The code is MIT-licensed on GitHub: the worker, the database schema and this website.

Verify.title: Integrity ledger
Verify.intro: Every flag, confirmation result, mitigation commitment, metered reading and monthly scorecard is written into an append-only hash chain, and the chain is time-stamped on Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps. Anyone can check that no record was changed after it was written.

check.title: Check the chain yourself
check.intro: Your browser downloads every entry, recomputes each SHA-256 hash and follows every link. Nothing on this page is taken on trust.
check.ok: All {n} entries check out, and {anchors, plural, =0 {no heads are stamped yet} one {# stamped head matches} other {# stamped heads match}}. Chain head:

broken.payload: Entry #{id}: its text does not match its hash.
broken.entry: Entry #{id}: its entry hash does not check out.
broken.link: Entry #{id}: it does not link to the entry before it.
broken.order: Entry #{id}: an entry is missing before it.
broken.anchor: The stamped head at entry #{id} does not match the chain.

anchors.title: Bitcoin anchors
anchors.intro: Each time the chain grows, its head is sent to two free OpenTimestamps calendars, which commit it to a Bitcoin block within hours. We then check each proof against that block's Merkle root.
anchors.none: No heads stamped yet; the first goes out on the next scheduled run.
anchors.pending: waiting for a block (usually a few hours)

how.title: Verify a proof without us
how.one: Download a head's .txt file and its .ots proof from the table above.
how.two: The .txt file holds the entry number and hash it stamps; the checker above shows the same hash for that entry.
how.three: Drop both files on <link>opentimestamps.org</link> (or run ots verify) to see the Bitcoin block that proves they existed at that time.

Verify.scope: The ledger holds no personal data: no names, emails, notes or report text. A timestamp proves a record existed and has not changed since; it does not turn a screening-grade figure into a verified one.

Sensors.title: Ground sensor network
Sensors.intro: Low-cost methane sensor nodes around each flagged landfill report every 10 minutes. A small model reads the pressure trend, the wind forecast and recent readings, and warns when a rise is likely in the next {h} hours. Falling air pressure pushes landfill gas out, so the warning can come before the level rises.
Sensors.simulatedNote: No sensors are installed yet. The nodes marked Simulated report from a physics-based simulator driven by real weather at each site, so the network, the warnings and the dashboard can be tested before hardware arrives. Simulated data never enters the integrity ledger and never emails anyone.

Sensors.warnText: A rise is likely within 3 hours ({p}).
Sensors.lelText: A reading reached {ppm} ppm, 10% of methane's lower explosive limit. Keep people and flames away and check on the ground.
Sensors.noAlerts: No alerts in the last 30 days.

System.title: How VayuNetra works, and how well
System.intro: The whole system on one page, with every accuracy figure behind it: the satellite model on held-out test sites, the India field test, and the sensor early-warning model.

system.title: The system

satellite.name: Sentinel-2 satellite
satellite.text: Free, every ~5 days. A U-Net AI with {params} million parameters reads {channels} input channels and the MBMP methane signal.

drone.name: Drone survey
drone.text: Flies over a flagged cell on demand to confirm the plume and map it at metre scale.

sensors.name: Ground sensor network
sensors.text: Five solar nodes per landfill, a reading every 10 minutes, each compared with an upwind background node.

gate.name: Physics gate
gate.text: Spectral and wind tests sort every flag into T1 methane-confident, T2 probable or T3 surface change.

confirm.name: Confirmation tracker
confirm.text: Every T1 or T2 flag opens a task: EMIT match, hyperspectral tasking, OGI drone or ground survey.

warning.name: Early-warning model
warning.text: A {weights}-weight network forecasts a methane rise {h} hours ahead from the pressure trend, the wind forecast and recent readings.

dashboard.name: Dashboard and alerts
dashboard.text: English and Hindi; emails to state officials; an action dossier per site.

ledger.name: Mitigation ledger
ledger.text: Who acts and by when, a capture calculator, metered tonnes.

scorecard.name: Public scorecard
scorecard.text: Monthly, per landfill, with CSV, JSON and GeoJSON downloads.

integrity.name: Integrity ledger
integrity.text: A hash chain of flags, results and readings, time-stamped on Bitcoin.

system.audience: Built for MoHUA, CPCB and state pollution control boards, and municipal corporations.

loop.title: From flag to verified reduction

detect.name: Detect
detect.text: Satellite AI flags T1, T2 or T3 on every new Sentinel-2 pass; ground sensors warn 3 hours ahead (simulated).

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.text: Each T1 or T2 flag opens a task: EMIT match, hyperspectral tasking, OGI drone or ground survey.

act.name: Act
act.text: The only step that removes tonnes: each measure has a named agency, a start date and expected tonnes (modelled).

verify.name: Verify
verify.text: Only metered gas counts as reduced; the satellite tracks the site's upper bound.

report.name: Report
report.text: A public scorecard every month, and every record in the Bitcoin-anchored ledger.

loop.back: If nothing changes after a measure, the loop goes back to Act with the next one.

acc.title: Accuracy
acc.intro: Every figure below is measured. The sensor model's figures are measured on simulated data and say so.

global.title: Satellite model on held-out test sites
global.intro: MethaneSET test split: sites the model never saw in training, compared with the classic MBMP method. Higher is better, except for false alarms.
global.far: False-alarm rate at the operating threshold
global.rateWithin: Emission rate: {share} of {plumes} real plumes within ±50% of the published MARS rate.
global.rateRatio: Median ratio to the published rate: {ratio} (1.00 means no bias).

matrix.title: Accuracy matrices at the operating threshold
matrix.intro: Rows are what was really there; columns are what the system said. Each share comes from the recall and false-alarm rate above, so these are rates, not counts.

india.title: India field test, January 2024 to December 2025
india.intro: Ghazipur, Bhalswa, Okhla, Deonar and Pirana, each with a control point {km} km away where no landfill is. A flag at a control point is a false alarm.
india.flagsNote: A flag is a scene scored above the threshold, before the physics gate sorts it.
india.tiers: Physics gate on the {flags} landfill flags: T1 {t1}, T2 {t2}, T3 {t3} ({burn} burn-like at Ghazipur).
india.perPass: Per-pass detection over dense Indian landfills: about {share} for plumes of {tph} t/h or more.
india.knownTruth: Known-truth test: the estimated rate was {ratio}× the injected rate at {tph} t/h.
india.bounds: Steady emission ruled out above (95%): Ghazipur {g}, Bhalswa {b}, Deonar {d}, Pirana {p}, Okhla {o} t/h.
india.fineTune: Fine-tuning on Indian backgrounds did not improve held-out detection (AUC about {auc}): the limit is the Sentinel-2 signal over dense cities, which is why VayuNetra is a two-tier system.

sensor.title: Sensor early-warning model (simulated)
sensor.intro: Trained and tested on simulated readings driven by real weather at the five landfills, tested on held-out Jul–Sep 2025. These numbers describe the simulator, not real air; the model is retrained once real nodes report.
sensor.weights: {n} weights; about {week} false warnings per node per week. Comparison: {other}.
sensor.try: Try the sensor network in the simulator →

limits.title: What these numbers do not show
limits.one: Every satellite estimate is screening-grade: confirm with a hyperspectral satellite, an OGI drone or a ground survey before enforcement or carbon crediting.
limits.two: On one pass at the operating threshold the satellite model catches about 3 in 10 plumes; repeated passes and the ground tier make up the rest.
limits.three: T2 and T3 flags are not methane detections: T2 is probable and needs confirmation, T3 is surface change rejected as methane.
limits.four: The sensor network is simulated until real nodes report; its figures will be re-measured on real readings.

proof.title: Proof
proof.intro: Flags, confirmation results, mitigation commitments, metered readings and monthly scorecards go into an append-only hash chain, time-stamped on Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps.

Simulator.title: Sensor network simulator
Simulator.intro: Five simulated solar sensor nodes around a landfill and the early-warning model, running in your browser. Change the weather, drag a sensor, open a crack in the landfill cover, and watch the forecast and the alerts respond.
Simulator.how: Every 10 simulated minutes each node takes a reading and the {weights}-weight model gives the chance that methane rises at that node within 3 hours. A warning opens when the chance reaches the model's alert threshold; a rise is a 30-minute mean 25 ppm above the background node.
Simulator.day: Day: mixing air spreads the plume
Simulator.night: Night: stable air keeps the plume low

map.label: Map of the landfill from above, with the simulated plume and the sensor nodes
map.legend: Methane above background at ground level
map.dragHint: Drag a sensor to move it, or select it and use the arrow keys.

tile.chance: Chance of a rise in 3 h:

controls.title: Weather and landfill
controls.trend: Pressure change over the next 3 hours
controls.sourceNote: A simulation input, not a measurement.

front.name: Pressure falling
front.text: A front arrives: pressure drops 2 hPa over the next 3 hours and pushes landfill gas out.

evening.name: Calm evening
evening.text: Light wind as the air turns stable after dark, so the plume stays near the ground.

windy.name: Windy, pressure rising
windy.text: Strong wind dilutes the plume and rising pressure holds the gas in.

leak.button: Open a crack in the cover
leak.note: No weather forecast sees a crack coming: the network catches it only as methane starts to climb.

forecast.title: Start from today's weather
forecast.hint: Wind, humidity and the pressure change over the next 3 hours from the Open-Meteo forecast, starting the clock now.
forecast.loaded: Today's weather at {site}, from the Open-Meteo forecast.
forecast.failed: The forecast could not be loaded; the controls are unchanged.

detail.title: {code}: {role}, {m} m from the centre
detail.excessChart: Methane above background, last 6 hours (ppm, 30-minute mean)
detail.chanceChart: Chance of a rise within 3 hours
detail.whyNote: Change in the chance, in percentage points, if this input were at its typical value. A simple test, not an exact breakdown.
detail.background: The background node measures the air arriving at the site, 3 km upwind. Every other node's reading is compared with it, as each satellite flag is compared with a control point.

log.title: Alerts in this run
log.empty: No alerts yet. Press play or pick a scenario.
log.warning: Early warning at {code}: {p} chance of a rise within 3 hours.
log.riseWarned: Methane {ppm} ppm above background at {code}, warned {min} minutes ahead.
log.riseUnwarned: Methane {ppm} ppm above background at {code}, with no warning before it.
log.noRise: Warning at {code} closed: no rise within 3 hours, a false alarm.
log.clear: {code} is back below the rise level.
log.leak: A crack opened in the landfill cover for 60 minutes.

Simulator.note: Simulated. No sensors are installed yet, so these readings come from a physics simulator, not real air. The forecast assumes the weather you set carries on for 3 hours. The model is the same {weights}-weight network the sensor dashboard runs, trained and tested on simulated readings (held-out ROC AUC {auc}); it is retrained once real nodes report.
Simulator.method: Physics: falling barometric pressure pushes landfill gas out and rising pressure holds it in (Kissas 2022; Xu et al. 2014); a Gaussian plume with daytime mixing and stable night air; a metal-oxide methane sensor with humidity and temperature effects, corrected by calibration (Furuta et al. 2024).

Ground.title: Ground network
Ground.intro: How a VayuNetra flag becomes a confirmed and fixed leak: the satellite finds the area, a wind forecast says where gas will go, solar LoRa nodes measure it, a Raspberry Pi at the site decides and sends SMS, and people confirm and fix it. Everything here is a simulation or a recorded test: no node has been built yet.

flow.title: The full flow
flow.intro: Eight steps, each with the code that runs it and the number that checks it. Select a step for the detail.

satellite.title: Satellite flag
satellite.runs: VayuNetra worker, every new Sentinel-2 pass
satellite.text: VayuNetra's U-Net scores each Sentinel-2 pass against four clean passes and the physics gate gives a tier. Re-run unchanged on the 33 cached Deonar passes, it flags 6 January 2025 again as T1 (score 0.853 against the 0.844 threshold) and flags nothing in 30 passes over the control point.

wind.title: Wind forecast
wind.runs: Chronos-2 on the Pi or in the cloud
wind.text: Chronos-2, zero-shot, forecasts the 10 m wind 12 hours ahead from the last 512 hours. Over a year of real ERA5 hours its 6-hour direction error is 19.5 degrees against 31.6 for repeating the last hour.

plan.title: Node plan
plan.text: The survey rings the fence at 150 m with 12, 8 or 6 nodes, puts the anemometer on the node nearest the gateway, a community node at the nearest school or hospital downwind and a background node 2.5 km upwind.

nodes.title: Solar LoRa nodes
nodes.runs: Heltec V3 on the carrier board
nodes.text: Each node samples gas every 10 s and reports every 5 minutes. A rise goes out at once as an alarm and is resent until the gateway acknowledges it. Below 25 % charge the gas heater is switched off.
nodes.checked: 118 firmware checks; compiles for the board

mesh.title: LoRa mesh
mesh.text: Every node relays a packet once; far nodes relay first and a heard relay cancels a waiting one. Around a 12-node ring the firmware delivered 99.8-100 % of reports, against 98.4-100 % in the hardware team's mesh model.
mesh.checked: Same ring as mesh.py, four radio settings

pi.title: Pi at the site
pi.text: The Pi stores every reading, calibrates it, compares each node with the background node, checks a rise against the wind, places the likely source and opens events.

sms.title: SMS and work orders
sms.text: Officials get one SMS per event in English or Hindi without needing internet. A work order closes only when downwind readings fall by half.

confirm.title: Confirmation
confirm.text: Every rise and source location is screening-grade: confirm on site with an OGI camera, a laser or a ground survey before enforcement. Confirmations become labels for retraining.

flow.filesText: Firmware: Vayu-node. Pi server: Vayu-server. Satellite model: VayuNetra worker. These pages run the firmware in your browser and the Pi's own Python on Vercel.

sim.title: Live simulation on the site
sim.intro: Every node here runs the real C firmware, compiled to WebAssembly, against models of its chips, the radio channel and the weather, at its planned place on the site. Turn the knobs; the gateway's output goes through the Pi's own detection and SMS code. Nothing is sent.
sim.failed: This browser could not start the firmware simulator.
sim.sourceHint: Click the map to move the leak.
sim.clickNode: Select a node to look inside it.
sim.pi: The Pi's code on those lines
sim.piStatus: {n} gateway lines, {a} readings accepted, {s} skipped. Nothing was sent.
sim.validateHelp: Runs a second copy of the firmware on the hardware team's landfill ring (12 nodes on a 300 x 200 m ellipse, gateway 450 m east, path-loss exponent 2.9) for two simulated hours at each radio setting, and compares the share of reports delivered with their recorded mesh results.
sim.basemapNote: Map: Mapbox. Node models are drawn 60 times life size so they show at site scale.
sim.screening: Screening-grade: simulated readings through the real firmware and the Pi's real code. A rise on the ground is confirmed on site before enforcement.

hw.title: Hardware and fabrication
hw.intro: The node as designed: the full assembly, the carrier board, the files a fab house needs, the pin map read from the PCB, and the circuit simulations, rerun live by the Pi's own Python.
hw.viewerHelp: Drag to turn, scroll to zoom.
hw.fabHelp: Gerbers and drill files for a 2-layer board, the KiCad project, the STEP assembly and the wiring list.
hw.pinsHelp: Read from vn_carrier.kicad_pcb, the board that gets fabricated, against the Heltec symbol's pin names. The firmware uses exactly this map.

find.hw_chk_heater: The gas heater draws 0.25 W, 5.9 Wh a day and most of the node's load. GPIO34 switches it through Q1, so the firmware turns it off below 25 % charge; R2 keeps it off until the firmware starts.
find.hw_chk_divider: The ADS1115's input (about 6 Mohm, the value in the team's ngspice model) loads the dividers: battery and 5 V rail read 0.83 % low, solar 1.86 % low. Near 25 % charge that is about 4 % of charge, so the firmware converts with the loaded ratio.
find.hw_chk_bme: GY-BME280 boards come strapped to address 0x76 or 0x77; the firmware tries both.
find.hw_chk_boost: The MT3608 boost has no enable pin, so its 8 mW also runs in deep sleep (0.19 Wh a day). The simulation includes it.
find.hw_chk_sleep: Anemometer pulses are counted by a GPIO interrupt, which does not run in light sleep, so the head node stays awake; the other nodes sleep between jobs.
find.hw_chk_socket: The Heltec socket footprint says to check the row spacing with calipers before ordering.

hw.firmwareText: {checks} checks pass. The node image uses {node} KB of flash and {ram} KB of RAM, the gateway {gw} KB. The simulator on the Live simulation page is the same C code in {wasm} KB of WebAssembly.
hw.simsHelp: Each one runs the hardware team's model through the Pi's Python on Vercel as you move the controls.
hw.gasHelp: TGS2600 resistance through the divider and RC filter into the ADS1115.
hw.droop: Supply droop during a LoRa burst
hw.droopHelp: Battery, protection and cable resistance against the Heltec's 0.19 A transmit pulse, with the particle sensor fan starting.
hw.energyHelp: Hour by hour on real weather: panel, cells, board current and the firmware's power policy.
hw.meshHelp: The hardware team's discrete-event mesh model: delivery, alarm bursts and latency by radio setting.
hw.apiFailed: The simulation service did not answer.

wind.title: Wind forecast
wind.intro: Which side of the site is downwind in the next hours decides which nodes should see a plume. The forecast model is a slot: Chronos-2 zero-shot now, VayuNetra's own fine-tuned Chronos-2 when it does better, and repeating the last hour as the fallback.
wind.backtestHelp: {n} forecasts per lead hour, issued every {every} h from {ctx} hours of history at {cells} ERA5 grid cells, {start} to {end}: after Chronos-2 was published, so it cannot have seen these hours. Truth: ERA5 10 m wind through the Open-Meteo archive API.
wind.summary: At {h} hours ahead the vector error falls from {p} to {c} m/s ({pct} % lower) and the direction error from {pd} to {cd} degrees.
wind.dir: Direction error, mean (degrees, wind at least 2 m/s)
wind.turningHelp: {n} forecast hours where the wind ended more than 45 degrees from the last observed hour. Repeating the last hour is wrong by construction there.
wind.bandHelp: Share of hours with both u and v inside Chronos-2's 10-90 % range. For independent u and v an honest range would hold about 64 %; below that the range is too narrow.
wind.sameCell: {a} and {b} fall in one ERA5 cell, so that cell is scored once.
wind.examplesHelp: Issued at evenly spaced times through the test year, not picked.
wind.liveHelp: Fetched {when} from the Open-Meteo forecast API: Chronos-2 on the last 30 days of the weather service's analysis, next to the weather service's own forecast. The Pi refreshes this itself; this page shows the saved run.
wind.note: Forecasts are screening-grade. A wrong direction makes the wind check say the pattern does not fit; it never hides a reading.

sat.title: Satellite layer: VayuNetra's model
sat.intro: VayuNetra's own plume model run again, unchanged, on every cached Sentinel-2 pass over Deonar and over its control point 5 km north. The worker's physics gate tiers each detection: T1 methane-confident, T2 probable, T3 surface change (rejected as methane).
sat.summary: {n} landfill passes: {d} detections ({t1} T1, {t2} T2, {t3} T3). Control point: {cd} of {cn} passes detected.
sat.scoresHelp: Each point is one cloud-light Sentinel-2 pass, compared with 4 clean passes 10-150 days away. Above the threshold the pass is a detection; the physics checks then decide its tier.
sat.compareHelp: The live worker took the overpass wind from ERA5-Land through Earth Engine; this run takes ERA5 from the Open-Meteo archive API. The detection and tier match; the rate moves with the wind.
sat.evidenceAlt: {date}: true colour, methane signal and plume mask with the wind
sat.toGround: What the ground network does with it
sat.toGroundText: A T1 or T2 flag becomes a hotspot in the site survey. The Live simulation puts the leak there by default, and the ring nodes sit where it blows. The ground nodes then say when and where gas rises between satellite passes.
